1.title: Backup and Recovery
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Backup and Recovery. It covers the exam area Monitor and maintain Azure resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Create a Recovery Services vault. Create an Azure Backup vault. Create and configure a backup policy. Perform backup and restore operations by using Azure Backup. Configure Azure Site Recovery for Azure resources. Perform a failover to a secondary region by using Site Recovery. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Monitor and maintain Azure resources (ten-fifteen percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Two vaults
1.text: Two vaults. The figure shows this: Azure Backup: a vault, a policy and protected items, and the two vault types.

1.title: Two vaults, continued
1.text: Two vaults. Recovery Services vault. Azure V Ms, files and folders (M A R S agent), sequel Server in V Ms, S A P H A N A, Azure Files; also hosts Site Recovery. Backup vault. Newer workloads: Azure Blobs, Azure Disks, Azure Database for Postgre sequel, Kubernetes. The vault must be in the same region as the V Ms it protects. Storage redundancy of the vault (L R S, Z R S (zone-redundant storage), G R S (geo-redundant storage)) is chosen before protecting items; G R S with cross-region restore lets you restore in the paired region. Exam tip: "Back up an Azure V M" equals a Recovery Services vault in the V M's region.

1.title: Backup policies
1.text: Backup policies. A backup policy sets when to back up and how long to keep each backup. Schedule. Daily or weekly, at a time you choose (some workloads more often). Retention. Daily, weekly, monthly, yearly retention points. Instant restore. Snapshots kept locally (one to five days) for fast restore. Soft delete. Deleted backup data is kept fourteen days by default and can be recovered.

1.title: Backup and restore operations
1.text: Backup and restore operations. Enable backup. Choose the vault, the policy and the V M(s); the first backup is full, later ones incremental. Backup now. On-demand backup. Restore a V M. Create new V M, Replace existing, or Restore disks (then build the V M from them). File recovery. Mount the recovery point and copy files without restoring the whole V M. Stop protection. Retain data (stop and keep) or delete it.

1.title: Azure Site Recovery (ASR)
1.text: Azure Site Recovery (A S R). Site Recovery gives disaster recovery: it replicates V Ms to a secondary region so you can fail over during an outage. Replication. Continuous replication of V M disks to the target region. Recovery plan. Ordered group of V Ms with steps and scripts for failover. Test failover. Validate the plan in an isolated network with no impact on production. Failover. Switch to the replica V Ms in the secondary region. Commit. Finalize the failover (the recovery point is the one used). Reprotect. Reverse replication from the secondary back toward the primary. Failback. Return to the original region.

1.title: Azure Site Recovery (ASR), continued
1.text: Azure Site Recovery (A S R). The figure shows this: Site Recovery: replicate, test failover, failover, reprotect and failback. Exam tip: Backup equals restore data from a point in time. Site Recovery equals keep a running replica in another region for failover. They are different and often used together.

1.title: Reports and alerts
1.text: Reports and alerts. Backup reports. Dashboards from Log Analytics data: usage, jobs, policies. Backup alerts. Built-in alerts for failed jobs and other events; route to email or action groups. Azure Monitor. Combine with metrics and alert rules. Exam tip: A Recovery Services vault must be in the same region as the V Ms it protects.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants to back up several Azure V Ms. What should be created first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A Recovery Services vault in the V Ms' region. V Ms are protected by a Recovery Services vault in the same region.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user deleted one file inside a V M. What is the fastest restore? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: File recovery by mounting a recovery point. File recovery copies individual files from a recovery point.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants V Ms replicated to another region so it can fail over during an outage. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Site Recovery. Site Recovery replicates V Ms for regional disaster recovery.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. How can the failover plan be validated without affecting production? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A test failover in an isolated network. Test failover is non-disruptive.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An administrator deletes a backup by mistake. How long can soft delete keep the data by default? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: fourteen days. Backup soft delete keeps data for fourteen days by default.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which vault protects Azure Blobs and Azure Disks? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Backup vault. Backup vaults protect the newer workloads.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which vault type hosts Site Recovery? Answer: A Recovery Services vault. Question two. What does a recovery plan do? Answer: Groups V Ms and orders their failover steps. Question three. What does reprotect do? Answer: Reverses replication after a failover.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the three V M restore options. Answer: Create new V M, replace existing, restore disks. Question five. What does instant restore use? Answer: Locally kept snapshots. Question six. Where do backup reports get their data? Answer: A Log Analytics workspace.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Vaults: Recovery Services (V Ms, files, sequel, Files, A S R); Backup vault (Blobs, Disks, Postgre sequel). Policy: schedule, retention, instant restore, soft delete fourteen days. Restore: new V M, replace, disks, file recovery. Site Recovery: replicate, recovery plan, test failover, failover, commit, reprotect, failback. Reports: backup reports (Log Analytics), backup alerts.
